title.narrative: Strengthening WASH Systems to Reduce Disease Outbreaks and Mitigate Impact of Seasonal Flooding in Bama IDPs Camp, Borno State, Northeast Nigeria.

description.narrative: ltpgtJami Al-Hakeem Foundation (J-HF) is submitting a project proposal under the 2025 First Standard Allocation Strategy, aimed at addressing and providing critical Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services for 32,682 persons in the GSSS Bama Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) Camp, Bama LGA, Borno State, Northeast Nigeria. The camp hosts approximately 84,850 displaced individuals across 34,999 households, including 20,746 women, 10,851 men, 31,873 boys, 32,713 girls, 21,200 children under five, and 180 persons living with disabilities.ltbrgtDespite the camp’s scale and vulnerability, WASH infrastructure remains severely inadequate, compounded by recurring seasonal flooding. These gaps have significantly increased the risk of waterborne disease outbreaks due to limited access to safe water, poor sanitation, and ineffective waste management systems.ltbrgtTo address these challenges, the proposed project will implement a comprehensive WASH intervention focused on enhancing service delivery, strengthening flood resilience, promoting hygiene practices, and supporting long-term public health outcomes.ltbrgtKey components include:ltbrgtlt/pgtltolgtltligtWater Supply Interventions: Daily trucking and distribution of 20,000 liters of chlorinated water for one month, followed by a transition to sustainable sources through the rehabilitation of one (1) existing water points, restoration of one solar-powered borehole, and construction of an additional two (2) solar-powered borehole. Additionally, two (3) handpump boreholes will be rehabilitated, and two new handpump units installed. Routine chlorination and maintenance will ensure water quality, supported by the training of Local Area Mechanics and provision of repair toolkits for rapid response and sustainability.lt/ligtltligtSanitation and Hygiene Enhancements: The project will construct 4 blocks of new gender-segregated latrines and rehabilitate 6 blocks of existing units to improve sanitation. Fifty strategically placed hand hygiene stations will be installed to promote infection prevention. Twenty trained Hygiene Promoters will lead community sensitization and behavior change campaigns, while 515 households will receive WASH and hygiene kits to support safe hygiene practices and disease prevention.lt/ligtltligtFlood Resilience and Waste Management: Robust waste collection and disposal protocols will be established to prevent environmental contamination during heavy rainfall. Monthly community-led environmental sanitation exercises will help address emerging WASH challenges, reduce public health risks, and strengthen the community’s resilience to floods and infrastructure disruptions.lt/ligtltligtProtection Mainstreaming: Gender-Based Violence (GBV) risk mitigation will be integrated across all components. This includes protection sensitization and mainstreaming, referral mechanisms, and psychosocial support to promote the safety, dignity, and well-being of vulnerable groups, particularly women and girls.lt/ligtlt/olgtltpgtThrough these integrated, community-driven WASH interventions, this project aims to safeguard the health, restore dignity, and enhance resilience for 32,682 directly and indirectly targeted populations in the GSSS Bama IDP Camp. Jami Al-Hakeem Foundation (J-HF) is committed to delivering sustainable solutions that will empower the 32,682 targeted population to better withstand future humanitarian and environmental shocks caused by flooding during the lean season.ltbrgtlt/pgt
